root_cause: The ov_generate_plugins_hpp() CMake function calls ov_target_link_plugins() which calls target_link_libraries() with MODULE_LIBRARY targets (openvino_auto_plugin, openvino_hetero_plugin, openvino_intel_cpu_plugin, openvino_intel_gpu_plugin, openvino_intel_npu_plugin, openvino_auto_batch_plugin). CMake does not allow linking MODULE_LIBRARY targets to other targets. This is a pre-existing code issue in cmake/developer_package/plugins/plugins.cmake line 275 affecting all Android builds (both x64 and arm64). The PR under test (mistune bump in docs/requirements.txt) did not introduce this issue - it is a persistent master-branch regression. This failure has been seen 12 times since 2026-08-08.
reproduction_steps: N/A - this reproduces on any Android CI build; not easily reproducible without the Android NDK toolchain setup.
recommended_actions: Investigate plugins.cmake:275 - the ov_target_link_plugins function must not use target_link_libraries with MODULE_LIBRARY targets on Android builds; consider using INTERFACE libraries or compile-time registration instead.
Check if a recent commit changed plugin build type from SHARED to MODULE and broke the Android linkage contract.
Search for the PR that introduced this regression (started 2026-08-08) and revert or fix it.
prevention_strategies: Add a CMake check in the Android CI pipeline that validates no MODULE_LIBRARY plugin targets are passed to target_link_libraries. Consider a precommit validation step for plugins.cmake changes.
historical_context: This exact failure has occurred 12 times since 2026-08-08, pattern 9ff022172665aa06. It is a persistent master-branch regression unrelated to individual PRs in the merge queue.
